changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led buyers, lead with this instead: "Your engineers can build a working flow in a weekend. One customer engineer built a working sitter payment flow from our docs and sandbox and showed it at Monday standup." Put the sandbox link in the first email and give champions a way to show a working flow to their VP within a day.
changes.why: The deal turned from a bake-off to 'no more if' after the customer's own engineer built a prototype from our docs and sandbox, so the proof is the build itself, not the claim of speed.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For engineering-led buyers stuck maintaining payments, open with the customer's words: "Payments shouldn't be a team. Stop babysitting this." Make local-currency expansion the supporting reason, not the opener.
changes.why: Expansion opened the door, but the pain was two engineers tied up on sitter payments, and the buyer described the problem as ownership and burden, not global growth.

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: Rewrite in the buyer's terms: "Sitter pay in the app, paid on time, in local currency, with identity checks built in." Swap in the buyer's own words for their side of the marketplace (e.g. 'sitters') and say 'the app' and 'pay' rather than 'marketplace' and 'payouts'.
changes.why: The marketplace piece landed, but the customer says 'the app' and 'sitter pay' and never 'marketplace' or 'payouts'.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with the generic authorization-uplift line in the default deck for low-ticket marketplaces (average order around $38). Bring it in only if the buyer raises acceptance rates themselves.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide drew silence, and the VP of Engineering said at a $38 average booking he was 'not losing sleep over auth rates'.
